facts.value: reunited with the Moscow Patriarchate in 2007, keeping broad autonomy

citations.excerpt: In 2007, the two groups reunited, but ROCOR retained broad autonomy in its affairs and administration.

facts.value: A Russian Orthodox church founded by bishops who left Russia after 1917, headquartered in New York after the Second World War, stressing Church Slavonic worship, traditional church order and a conservative theological outlook.

citations.excerpt: After WWII, its worldwide headquarters moved from Yugoslavia to New York.

From the very beginning, ROCOR had a strong emphasis on preserving Russian culture, the Slavic style of Orthodox Christian worship (with Church Slavonic as the principal language of services), traditional church order, a conservative theological outlook
